Don't know if any of this applies to you or is otherwise useful information, but here it goes. I used to smoke on a daily basis for 5-7 years I think, but for the most part I rarely smoked during the day. It was a wind down thing for me when the daily duties had been taken care of. My motivation for stopping was needing a clear head because I was going back to school. Now anyone that says you aren't getting dumber by smoking are out of their mind and usually don't have a 'sober' baseline to compare with either. You are getting dumber, period! That said, it's not a point of no return as you'll soon discover. So chin up, there's a reward around the corner.

As for withdrawal symptoms I found them very much to be in line with my smoking habit. I felt absolutely no craving during the day, but come nighttime were I'd be used to have a buzz on something was missing. I wont say I was craving a blunt, but I could definitely feel my usual 'sleeping medicine' wasn't there. It passed over in about a months time though, but be prepared you could face similar issues. You might also get some pretty funky dreams during that time.

As for kicking bad habits in general, it's a really good idea to have a distraction handy should the urge arise. Something like snake or tetris on your phone is excellent in that respect. As a bonus you might end up getting really fucking good at it too:)
